plausibility.causal_story: Tumour PD-L1 (CD274) transcription in NSCLC is largely interferon-driven through JAK/STAT1, and the same interferon axis is what LKB1 loss disables via STING silencing (C-029/C-030) and what supplies CXCL9/10 for T-cell recruitment. A tumour carrying an STK11 mutation that nonetheless expresses PD-L1 at TPS ≥50% therefore has, by that chain, a functionally intact interferon response — because the variant does not abolish kinase activity, because the second allele is retained, or because a compensating route keeps the axis on. In such tumours the substrate that PD-1 blockade acts on (a pre-existing, interferon-driven, PD-L1-marked T-cell response under checkpoint restraint) is present, so the mutation should not mark resistance; in the PD-L1-low bands it should. The chain predicts both the direction (null in the high band) and the specificity (a gradient across bands, with PD-L1 superseding genotype), and it is falsified by a clear STK11 penalty at TPS ≥50%.
mechanism_steps: STING silencing after LKB1 loss removes tumour-intrinsic type I interferon output (C-029/C-030).
Interferon signalling through JAK/STAT1 is the principal inducer of tumour CD274 expression and of CXCL9/CXCL10.
Hence STK11-mutant tumours are systematically PD-L1-low and T-cell-poor (C-006, C-041, C-050, C-007) — PD-L1 is a functional readout of the axis, not an independent marker.

An STK11-mutant tumour with TPS ≥50% is therefore one in which the axis is intact, i.e. the mutation has not produced the functional deficiency (consistent with C-034, phenotype rather than mutation).
In that group PD-1 blockade has the substrate it needs, so survival should not differ from STK11 wild-type.
In the PD-L1-low bands the deficiency is present, so the penalty should appear — a gradient across bands, not a uniform effect.
alternative_explanations: The PD-L1-high stratum is smaller, so a null is a wide interval rather than an absence of effect; the claim requires an equivalence-style reading of the estimate, not just p > 0.05.
PD-L1-high STK11-mutant tumours differ on other grounds — histology, specimen site, prior radiation, time from biopsy — that independently predict better survival.
The contrary direct evidence: In Vivo 2020 reports lower ORR with low STK11/LKB1 expression specifically among TPS ≥50% tumours, which is the same stratum and the opposite direction.
confounding_risks: Conditioning on PD-L1 conditions on a downstream consequence of the exposure, so within-band comparison can induce collider bias if an unmeasured factor raises both PD-L1 and survival; the estimate is a controlled direct effect and should be labelled as one.
Assay heterogeneity: clone, platform and archival drift move patients across the 50% threshold non-randomly, and misallocation is likely differential by institution and era.
Indication bias: first-line monotherapy at TPS ≥50% is preferentially given to older, frailer or lower-burden patients, while fitter patients with bulky disease receive chemo-immunotherapy.
Prognostic vs predictive: without a chemotherapy comparator in the same stratum, a null is consistent both with 'no predictive effect' and with a prognostic effect offset by something else.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry, plus the requirement that a PD-L1 result predates treatment, which selects on workup completeness.
Panel ascertainment: STK11 callability and variant-classification thresholds differ across assays, and the null is exactly the result that exposure misclassification would manufacture.

feasibility.cohort_derivation: Recorded because the power conclusion CHANGED from the prior run and the change matters. REAL: 2665 NSCLC patients received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent, of whom 336 STK11-LoF (12.6%). DERIVED: x0.65 first-line (A2) x0.35 monotherapy (A3) x0.85 EGFR/ALK exclusion (A1) = ~515 first-line ICI-monotherapy patients, ~65 STK11-LoF against ~450 wildtype. Applying the binary PD-L1 restriction that is the closest available approximation to the intended population (ascertained AND positive, ~60% of the monotherapy group) would leave ~39 against ~270. The prior formula-derived run put this at ~121 mutant against ~739 wildtype, roughly double, from a cohort-wide monotherapy figure and a 14.1% prevalence; both were optimistic.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: 1.62 at f=0.6 before any PD-L1 restriction; 1.86 after — against an equivalence claim

power.estimand: STK11 hazard ratio within the PD-L1 TPS >= 50% first-line monotherapy stratum, framed as an EQUIVALENCE claim ('is not associated with shorter overall survival'). An equivalence claim needs tighter precision than a difference claim, not looser.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; illustrative figures at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: Unrestricted first-line monotherapy (65 vs 450): sum of inverse patient counts 0.01761, SE(log HR) = 0.210 / 0.171 / 0.148 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, minimum detectable HR = 1.80 / 1.62 / 1.51, and the 95% interval half-width at f = 0.6 is 0.336, i.e. an equivalence bound of roughly 0.72-1.40 around a null point estimate. With the binary PD-L1 restriction applied (39 vs 270) the bound widens to roughly 0.65-1.54. THIS IS A CHANGE FROM THE PRIOR RUN, which derived SE 0.126 and a bound of 0.78-1.28 and concluded 'power adequate, population unconstructible'. On the real counts the bound of 0.72-1.40 is barely narrower than Papillon-Cavanagh's published 0.76-1.67, and the PD-L1-restricted bound of 0.65-1.54 is not narrower at all. Power now fails too.
power.adequacy: Inadequate on both counts, where the prior run found only one. The population cannot be constructed, AND the equivalence bound the real cohort would support (roughly 0.72-1.40 unrestricted, 0.65-1.54 restricted) does not materially improve on the published intervals this hypothesis was written to tighten. The prior run's more generous conclusion — that the cohort could answer the question if only it recorded PD-L1 — does not survive the real treatment counts.

measurement_concerns: The tempting workaround is refused explicitly. First-line ICI monotherapy is in practice given almost exclusively at TPS >= 50%, so 'received first-line monotherapy' could stand in for the PD-L1 restriction. That substitutes a prescribing decision for a measurement, imports every determinant of regimen choice (age, frailty, disease burden, institution, era) into the stratum definition, makes an unverifiable assumption about the very threshold the hypothesis is about, and destroys the band gradient entirely, since the 1-49% and <1% strata have no monotherapy analogue.

A binary NLP PD-L1 flag would make the population-defining variable nlp_extracted, which for a hypothesis whose entire content is the PD-L1 threshold is a primary-exposure-level weakness, not a covariate-level one.

The hypothesis predicts a null, and exposure misclassification from panel_version-dependent STK11 callability would manufacture exactly that result. An equivalence claim needs its exposure measured better than a difference claim does.

Conditioning on PD-L1 would have been conditioning on a downstream consequence of the exposure, a controlled direct effect open to collider bias. Stage 3 referred this; recorded even though the analysis cannot run.
feasibility.reject_reason: The population is defined by a measurement the dataset does not make, and — a change from the prior assessment — power now fails independently as well. On the field: PD-L1 exists in this schema for the first time, as pdl1_sample_nlp and pdl1_history_nlp, but as binary NLP-derived positive/negative flags. H-008 is not a hypothesis about NSCLC with a PD-L1 covariate; it is a hypothesis about the TPS >= 50% stratum specifically and about the gradient across <1%, 1-49% and >=50%. A binary positive pools 1-49% with >=50%, so substituting it would silently redefine the population as PD-L1 >=1%, where the premise (high PD-L1 marks an intact interferon axis and hence a functionally non-deficient STK11 mutant) simply does not hold. Three of the hypothesis's own covariates — assay, clone, specimen-to-treatment interval — are equally absent, and the pdl1 fields are not even declared in the schema's tables section. On power: the prior formula-derived run concluded the cohort was large enough and died only on measurement. The real treatment counts halve that stratum — 2665 ICI-treated NSCLC patients, 336 STK11-LoF, giving ~65 mutant against ~450 wildtype after the first-line, monotherapy and driver restrictions — and the equivalence bound at an assumed 60% event fraction is roughly 0.72-1.40, against Papillon-Cavanagh's published 0.76-1.67. That is not the advance the hypothesis promised, and applying any PD-L1 restriction widens it to 0.65-1.54, which is no advance at all. Using receipt of first-line monotherapy as a proxy for TPS >= 50% is declined: it replaces a measurement with a prescribing decision and cannot produce the low and intermediate bands the gradient prediction requires. Paired-prereg consequence: H-007 fails on the same field, so stage 3's joint-interpretation instruction lapses cleanly rather than leaving a surviving half to reinterpret.

hypotheses.statement: The association between STK11 loss-of-function and shorter overall survival on ICI-containing therapy is present in KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and absent in KRAS-wildtype lung adenocarcinoma, i.e. there is a KRAS-by-STK11 interaction on survival.

origin.rationale: The mechanism is the point, and it is specific rather than a co-occurrence observation. Kitajima showed that LKB1 loss silences STING through DNMT1 and EZH2 hyperactivation driven by elevated S-adenosylmethionine (C-029, C-030), and did so in a KRAS-driven context: the one-carbon and serine-glycine flux that raises SAM is downstream of oncogenic KRAS-driven anabolic metabolism. On that account LKB1 loss without an activating KRAS allele does not generate the methyl-donor surplus needed to hyperactivate the methyltransferases, so STING is retained and the tumour is not rendered innately blind. That predicts a conditional, not an additive, effect. The clinical shape already matches: Ricciuti reports STK11 and KEAP1 worsen ICI outcomes among KRAS-mutant but not KRAS-wildtype LUAD (C-015 versus C-016) and that the distinct immunophenotype appears only in KRAS-mutant tumours (C-017), and the gap report classifies this pair as an effect modifier rather than a contradiction. What is missing is a formal interaction term estimated with enough KRAS-wildtype STK11-mutant patients to distinguish a true null from an underpowered subgroup — that stratum is small in every published cohort and large in a modern clinicogenomic one.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Reported the stratified result this hypothesis formalises, concluding that STK11 and KEAP1 confer worse outcomes among KRAS-mutant but not KRAS-wildtype LUAD. The stratified finding is therefore published; what is not published is a formal interaction test with a confidence interval on the interaction term, which is what distinguishes a real effect modification from two subgroups of different size.

Examined STK11/KEAP1/SMARCA4 co-mutations in RAS-activated but KRAS-wildtype metastatic NSCLC on ICIs and reported that the adverse association seen in KRAS-mutant disease was not clearly observed in the KRAS-wildtype population. A second, independent null in the KRAS-wildtype stratum, consistent with the predicted interaction but reducing the novelty of the stratified claim.

Did not stratify by KRAS and found no STK11-by-treatment interaction overall; if the KRAS-by-STK11 interaction is real, pooling across KRAS strata is one explanation for that null, which makes the two results compatible rather than contradictory.

The comparison of interest is the difference between the STK11 effect inside and outside the KRAS-mutant stratum.

inclusion: KRAS and STK11 both callable on the sequencing panel used
exclusion: EGFR-activating mutation or ALK/ROS1 fusion, which populate the KRAS-wildtype stratum with a distinct biology and would fake an interaction

plausibility.causal_story: Oncogenic KRAS drives glycolytic, glutaminolytic and serine-glycine one-carbon flux, which raises the S-adenosylmethionine pool. In the absence of LKB1/AMPK restraint that surplus hyperactivates DNMT1 and EZH2 (C-030), which methylate and silence STING (C-029), removing cytosolic dsDNA sensing and type I interferon output, reducing CXCL9/10 and CD8 recruitment (C-007) and leaving PD-1 blockade with little to release. Without an activating KRAS allele the methyl-donor surplus is not generated, the methyltransferases are not hyperactivated, STING is retained, and LKB1 loss does not render the tumour innately blind. The effect of STK11 loss is therefore conditional on KRAS rather than additive, and the product term — not two subgroup estimates — is the estimand. The falsifiable step is the KRAS-dependence of the SAM surplus: if LKB1 loss raises SAM in KRAS-wildtype tumours too, the interaction is null.
mechanism_steps: Oncogenic KRAS increases serine-glycine and one-carbon flux, raising the intracellular SAM pool.
LKB1 loss removes AMPK-dependent restraint on that anabolic program, so SAM accumulates further.
Elevated SAM hyperactivates DNMT1 and EZH2 (C-030, cell line).
DNMT1/EZH2 activity silences STING, abolishing cytosolic dsDNA sensing (C-029).
Type I interferon output falls, lowering CXCL9/CXCL10 and CD8 infiltration (C-007, human ex vivo; C-017, KRAS-mutant-only immunophenotype).
In KRAS-wildtype tumours steps 1-3 do not occur, STING is retained, and STK11 loss carries no comparable immune penalty — a positive KRAS x STK11 interaction on survival.
alternative_explanations: The KRAS-wildtype stratum is a mixture of MET exon 14, BRAF, RET and ERBB2-driven and never-smoker biologies with their own prognosis and ICI sensitivity, so an apparent interaction may be driver composition rather than KRAS-dependence.
Differential exposure quality: STK11 events in KRAS-wildtype tumours may less often be biallelic or clonal, so the interaction could be H-014's zygosity effect appearing in KRAS clothing.
The published 'absent in KRAS-wildtype' result is a nonsignificance claim in the smaller stratum; the interaction may be an artefact of unequal precision rather than unequal effect.
confounding_risks: Smoking: KRAS-mutant LUAD is heavily smoking-enriched and KRAS-wildtype LUAD is not, so stratifying on KRAS is partly stratifying on smoking, with all its prognostic baggage.
Prognostic vs predictive: no non-ICI arm, so a real KRAS-by-STK11 interaction may exist on chemotherapy too (C-037 shows a large STK11 effect with no ICI present) and would not be ICI-specific.
PD-L1 distribution differs between KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype disease, and PD-L1 is partly downstream of the same interferon axis, so adjusting for it is adjusting for a mediator.
KEAP1 co-mutation frequency differs by KRAS status, so the interaction can be carried by KEAP1 unless modelled jointly (see H-002).
Panel ascertainment: KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal while STK11 coverage is not, so the four genotype cells are not equally well measured.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry, plus the exclusion of EGFR/ALK, which reshapes the KRAS-wildtype reference cell.

missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS band — missing as a band; binary NLP flag available. Listed as a covariate, and its absence is arguably a benefit here: stage 3 noted PD-L1 sits downstream of the same interferon axis as the exposure, so adjusting for it would have been mediator adjustment. Drop the term and say so in the prereg; do not substitute the binary flag without declaring the change of estimand.

Gene-by-panel coverage map — panel_version exists with a real distribution, but which versions call STK11 is not stated. KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal across all four IMPACT panels while STK11 coverage is not, so the four genotype cells are not equally well ascertained and the smallest cell is the most exposed to it. External coverage manifest required on the cohort spec; restricted denominator reported before locking.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Anchored throughout on real counts. REAL: kras_any_alteration 2195, stk11_loss_of_function 716, kras_and_stk11lof_comutant 385 — so the KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell, which is the cell every published cohort calls 'null' without being able to distinguish null from underpowered, is a real 716 - 385 = 331 across NSCLC. KRAS-mutant/STK11-LoF-negative = 1810; KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF-negative = 5283. REAL ICI-exposure rates, computed from by_treatment_exposure rather than assumed: 46.9% for STK11-LoF (336/716) and 32.8% for STK11-wildtype (2329/7093). Applying those gives ICI-treated cells of 181 / 594 / 155 / 1733 (summing correctly to the real 336 and 2329). DERIVED restrictions: adenocarcinoma (x0.92 on the KRAS-mutant cells, which are LUAD-concentrated; x0.70 on the KRAS-wildtype cells), EGFR/ALK exclusion (x0.99 on KRAS-mutant, x0.72 on KRAS-wildtype, since activating EGFR and ALK events are essentially all KRAS-wildtype), first-line A2 (x0.65 throughout). ANALYSABLE, first-line: KRAS-mut/STK11-LoF 107, KRAS-mut/STK11-wt 352, KRAS-wt/STK11-LoF 51, KRAS-wt/STK11-wt 568. ANY-LINE variant (dividing out A2): 165 / 542 / 78 / 874. The 51-patient KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell contributes 58% of the interaction variance and is the entire design.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: KRAS-by-STK11 ratio-of-hazard-ratios 1.94 at f=0.6 first-line; 1.71 at f=0.6 any-line

power.estimand: KRAS x STK11 product term on overall survival — the ratio of the STK11 hazard ratio inside the KRAS-mutant stratum to the STK11 hazard ratio outside it. Per R5b this is an interaction and must be pre-registered as one (--estimand interaction --interaction-with KRAS status); two stratified subgroup hazard ratios reported side by side are NOT this quantity and are the error the hypothesis was written to correct.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, reference 0.6.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: FIRST-LINE (cells 107 / 352 / 51 / 568), sum of inverse patient counts 0.03356: SE(log ROR) = 0.290 / 0.236 / 0.205 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, minimum detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios = 2.25 / 1.94 / 1.78. ANY-LINE with line entered as a covariate (cells 165 / 542 / 78 / 874), sum 0.02187: SE = 0.234 / 0.191 / 0.165, minimum detectable ratio = 1.93 / 1.71 / 1.59. Prior formula-derived run reported 1.70 at f = 0.6 on an 86-patient KRAS-wildtype/STK11-mutant cell; the real first-line-restricted cell is 51 and the figure moves to 1.94.
conditions: THE ANY-LINE SPECIFICATION IS REQUIRED, with line_of_therapy entered as a covariate rather than as a restriction. This is a change to the population as stage 2 wrote it ('first-line ICI-containing therapy') and must be recorded as such in the cohort spec and prereg, not made silently. It is necessary: restricting to first line costs 35% of every cell and moves the minimum detectable interaction from 1.71 to 1.94, which is above most of the range the literature implies. The sensitivity figures above are quoted for the any-line specification; the first-line figures are in the narrative.

Prespecify in advance that a null interaction below a ratio-of-hazard-ratios of 1.7 is INCONCLUSIVE and must not be reported as evidence that the STK11 effect is unconditional on KRAS. Reporting it that way would repeat, at larger scale and with more authority, exactly the null-versus-underpowered confusion this hypothesis exists to resolve — which would be worse than not running it.

Model KEAP1 jointly. KEAP1 co-mutation frequency differs by KRAS status (real: 512 of 1013 STK11-altered patients also carry KEAP1), so an uncontrolled interaction can be carried by KEAP1. This makes H-009 and H-002 share a panel-coverage restriction and they should use the same one.

Record and handle the non-KRAS drivers occupying the KRAS-wildtype cell (MET, BRAF, RET, ERBB2) explicitly. They are callable from genomic_variant.hugo_symbol subject to panel coverage, and their coverage varies by panel_version more than KRAS's does — so the exclusion is executable but its completeness is panel-dependent and must be reported.
Left-truncate risk-set entry at days_dx_to_sequencing and report the truncation-interval distribution by genotype cell.
power.adequacy: Adequate for the upper half of the range the literature implies, and honestly marginal below it. Ricciuti's stratified pattern (STK11 HR roughly 1.6-2.0 among KRAS-mutant against ~1.0 among KRAS-wildtype) implies a ratio-of-hazard-ratios of roughly 1.6-2.0. The any-line design detects 1.71 at f = 0.6 and 1.59 at f = 0.8, so it can resolve the upper part of that range and cannot resolve the lower part; the first-line-restricted design at 1.94 can barely resolve any of it, which is why the any-line specification is made a condition rather than a suggestion. What tips this to a pass rather than an underpowered rejection is that the real KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell is 331 patients cohort-wide — larger than any published cohort's, and the specific cell whose emptiness makes the existing literature uninterpretable. The design improves on the state of the art even where it cannot settle the question, provided the 1.7 inconclusiveness bound is carried in writing.

measurement_concerns: Both the exposure and the modifier are variant calls — the strongest ascertainment this schema offers, and the reason this hypothesis survives while the NLP-modified ones do not.

MNAR co-mutation is asymmetric here in the worst possible direction: KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal across IMPACT341/410/468/505 while STK11 coverage is not, so the KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell — already the smallest at 51 analysable patients — is also the one most likely to be depleted by callability, and 'STK11-wildtype' in the older panels mixes true wildtype with never-tested. Restrict to panels calling both; the real panel distribution bounds the cost at 4.2% (IMPACT341 only) to 21.3% (IMPACT341 + IMPACT410).

smoking_status is nlp_extracted, and KRAS-mutant LUAD is heavily smoking-enriched (real: 5438 ever-smokers against 2027 never-smokers in NSCLC), so stratifying on KRAS is partly stratifying on a variable measured with unknown error. It is a covariate here, not the exposure.
genomic_callable is 7476/7809; the 4.3% without usable genomic ascertainment are excluded, not imputed wild-type.

Left truncation at days_dx_to_sequencing required. ICI-only design, so a positive interaction is prognostic until a non-ICI arm says otherwise — and the schema DOES support such an arm (2007 NSCLC platinum-no-ICI-ever patients, of whom a real 163 are STK11-LoF), which is H-001's design. A future version of H-009 crossed with that arm would be the strongest hypothesis in the file; it is not this one.

hypotheses.statement: Among STK11-loss-of-function advanced non-squamous NSCLC patients, first-line platinum-doublet plus anti-PD-1 is associated with longer overall survival than first-line anti-PD-1 monotherapy, and the advantage of adding chemotherapy is larger in STK11-mutant than in STK11-wildtype patients.

origin.rationale: The graph's treatment coverage is lopsided — 22 claims on ICI monotherapy against 9 on chemo-immunotherapy — and the head-to-head question clinicians actually face has never been asked of either arm. The mechanism gives a directional prediction rather than a hedge. LKB1 loss silences STING-dependent innate priming (C-029, C-030) and compromises immunoproteasome-dependent antigen presentation (C-031); both are the steps by which PD-1 blockade alone converts a pre-existing T-cell response into tumour control. When those steps are broken, a checkpoint antibody has little to release, which fits the PD-L1-low, T-cell-poor phenotype (C-006, C-041, C-050). Platinum chemotherapy does not depend on either step for its direct cytotoxic effect. So the expected pattern is that STK11-mutant patients lose relatively more by having chemotherapy withheld than wild-type patients do. Notably this is the opposite framing from the trial literature, which asks whether adding the ICI to chemotherapy still helps; that question already has a randomized answer, and this one does not, because no trial randomizes monotherapy against chemo-immunotherapy within an STK11 stratum. It is precisely a real-world treatment-selection contrast.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: J Clin Oncol 43 (16_suppl) e20504, ASCO 2025 abstract
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Meta-analysis of six randomized and one comparative study (1596 patients) found chemo-immunotherapy retained OS benefit over chemotherapy alone despite STK11 (HR 0.80, 0.67-0.97), KEAP1 (0.76) and KRAS (0.67) mutation. This closes the adjacent question — whether adding an ICI to chemotherapy still works in STK11-mutants — and any hypothesis phrased that way should not be proposed. It does not touch the monotherapy-versus-chemo-immunotherapy contrast proposed here.

In the 54 STK11-mutant patients, adding pembrolizumab to chemotherapy gave PFS HR 0.81 (0.44-1.47) and OS HR 0.75 (0.37-1.50) — both nonsignificant, against PFS HR 0.38 in wild-type. An underpowered subgroup that is routinely read as evidence of resistance; it constrains the size of any incremental-ICI effect but says nothing about withholding chemotherapy.

Reports that STK11/KEAP1-altered NSCLC is relatively resistant to standard PD-(L)1-plus-chemotherapy combinations and that adding CTLA-4 blockade abrogates that resistance. This weakens the present hypothesis materially: if chemo-immunotherapy is itself compromised in STK11-mutants, the predicted advantage over monotherapy may be small. Recorded because it cuts against the candidate.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: WCLC 2018 abstract MA19.10 (J Thorac Oncol S1556-0864(18)31439-4)
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Reported progressive disease as best response in 37.5% of STK11/LKB1-altered versus 6.1% of wild-type patients on chemo-immunotherapy. A conference abstract that never became a full paper — the classic grave for this kind of result — and it argues chemo-immunotherapy is also poor in STK11-mutants.

exposure.description: First-line platinum-doublet plus anti-PD-1/PD-L1 in STK11-loss-of-function patients
exposure.genomic_criteria: STK11 nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, homozygous deletion, or oncogenic/likely-oncogenic missense
exposure.treatment_criteria: first-line regimen containing both a platinum agent and an anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent started within 28 days of one another

comparator.description: STK11-loss-of-function patients receiving first-line anti-PD-1/PD-L1 monotherapy with no platinum agent, with the same regimen contrast among STK11-wildtype patients as the second stratum; the estimand is the regimen-by-STK11 interaction, and both arms are restricted to a PD-L1 band in which both regimens are genuinely used so the contrast is not pure confounding by indication.

population.description: Adults with advanced non-squamous NSCLC receiving first-line ICI-containing therapy with PD-L1 recorded and panel sequencing covering STK11
inclusion: PD-L1 TPS recorded before first-line therapy
first-line regimen class unambiguously classifiable as monotherapy or chemo-immunotherapy
exclusion: PD-L1 TPS <50%, where monotherapy is rarely used and the comparison would be confounded by indication

proposed_covariates: PD-L1 TPS as a continuous term within the restricted band
ECOG performance status, the dominant driver of regimen choice
treating site and calendar year of treatment start
propensity for regimen assignment as a sensitivity analysis, since confounding by indication is the central threat here

plausibility.causal_story: PD-1 blockade works by removing a brake on an existing, primed, MHC-I-restricted CD8 response. Both the innate licence for that priming (STING/type I interferon, C-029/C-030) and the peptide supply that feeds it (immunoproteasome, C-031) are degraded by LKB1 loss, which is why STK11-mutant tumours are PD-L1-low and T-cell-poor (C-006, C-041, C-050). Platinum's direct cytotoxic effect — DNA adducts, replication-fork collapse, apoptosis — does not require either step. Withholding chemotherapy therefore removes the one reliably active modality in an STK11-mutant tumour while leaving an antibody with little to release, whereas in a wild-type tumour monotherapy still has a working immune substrate. Prediction: the survival advantage of chemo-immunotherapy over monotherapy is larger in STK11-mutants, i.e. a positive regimen-by-STK11 interaction.
mechanism_steps: LKB1 loss silences STING and removes type I interferon-dependent licensing of priming (C-029/C-030).
LKB1 loss compromises immunoproteasome activity and raises autophagic flux, reducing MHC-I peptide supply (C-031).
PD-1 blockade alone therefore has little pre-existing response to release in STK11-mutant tumours, consistent with their PD-L1-low, T-cell-poor phenotype.
Platinum kills tumour cells by direct DNA damage, a route that does not require STING sensing or immunoproteasome function.
Hence the incremental value of the chemotherapy component is greater in STK11-mutant than in STK11-wildtype tumours.
Prediction: regimen-by-STK11 interaction favouring chemo-immunotherapy in the mutant stratum, estimated within a PD-L1 band where both regimens are genuinely used.
alternative_explanations: Genotype-aware prescribing: as STK11/KEAP1 status became routinely reported, clinicians began preferring chemo-immunotherapy for STK11-mutants, so the interaction can be manufactured by treatment selection that is itself a function of the exposure.

Platinum's contribution in combination is partly immunogenic cell death, which depends on the same sensing and presentation machinery — so the premise that the chemotherapy limb is LKB1-independent may be false, and the true interaction smaller or absent (consistent with Skoulidis 2024).

KEAP1/NRF2 co-mutation confers platinum resistance, so in the co-mutated subset the chemotherapy limb is blunted too and the interaction is diluted by co-mutation composition rather than by STK11 biology.
confounding_risks: Confounding by indication is the central threat and it is not removed by restricting to TPS ≥50%: within that band, chemo-immunotherapy is chosen for bulky, symptomatic, rapidly progressing disease while monotherapy is chosen for frail or lower-burden patients. These push the comparison in opposite directions and neither is well captured.

Exposure-dependent treatment assignment: if genotype is known before regimen choice, selection is a function of STK11 itself, which is precisely the route to a spurious interaction. Sequencing turnaround relative to treatment start must be modelled, not assumed.
Calendar trend: the strength of genotype-aware prescribing rises by year, so a year-by-regimen-by-genotype structure lurks behind any interaction estimate.
ECOG is recorded coarsely and inconsistently in real-world data yet is the dominant determinant of regimen intensity.
Prognostic vs predictive: both arms contain an ICI, so this compares two active regimens; it cannot establish that the STK11 effect is immune-mediated rather than a chemosensitivity effect.
Immortal time: patients must survive to receive and be sequenced for the index regimen, and the truncation interval differs between regimen groups.

required_fields: PD-L1 tumour proportion score, thresholded at >=50% and then modelled continuously within the band — the restriction that makes the regimen contrast interpretable
missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS >= 50% AS A RESTRICTION — missing. The binary NLP flags cannot supply it, and here the substitution is not merely imprecise, it is self-defeating. The hypothesis excludes TPS <50% in its own words 'where monotherapy is rarely used and the comparison would be confounded by indication'. A binary 'positive' includes the 1-49% band, which is exactly the band where monotherapy is rarely used — so restricting to binary-positive readmits the population the restriction exists to remove and reinstates the confounding the design was built to defuse. The design's only stated defence against its own central threat is unavailable.

Treating site / institution — listed as a covariate ('treating site and calendar year of treatment start'). first_contact_year supplies the year; no site or institution identifier exists in any table. Site is a determinant of regimen preference and of how early genotype-aware prescribing was adopted, which is the exposure-dependent-assignment threat.

Comorbidity and frailty measures beyond nlp_extracted ECOG — the dominant determinants of monotherapy versus chemo-immunotherapy choice, and the ones the propensity-score sensitivity analysis the hypothesis proposes would need.
A table/field declaration for the pdl1 flags — present only in cohort_counts, not in `tables`.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Carried far enough to show that power fails independently. REAL: 336 NSCLC patients are both ICI-exposed and STK11-LoF; 2329 are ICI-exposed and STK11-wildtype. DERIVED: x0.65 first-line (A2) x0.85 non-squamous and EGFR/ALK exclusion = 186 STK11-LoF and 1287 STK11-wildtype on first-line ICI-containing therapy. Splitting by regimen at the assumed 35/65 monotherapy/chemo-immunotherapy ratio (A3) gives STK11-LoF 65 monotherapy and 121 chemo-immunotherapy, STK11-wildtype 450 and 837. The design then requires the TPS >= 50% restriction, which would remove most of the chemo-immunotherapy arm (assume 30% retained, since chemo-immunotherapy is given across all PD-L1 bands while monotherapy is concentrated in the high band): ~36 and ~251. The four interaction cells are therefore roughly 65 / 36 / 450 / 251.

power.estimand: regimen-by-STK11 interaction on overall survival within a restricted PD-L1 band — the ratio of the chemo-immunotherapy-versus-monotherapy hazard ratio in STK11-mutants to the same contrast in STK11-wildtype patients.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8. These figures assume the PD-L1 restriction could be applied, which it cannot; they exist only to show that power is a second, independent objection.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: Cells 65 / 36 / 450 / 251, sum of inverse patient counts 0.04937: SE(log ROR) = 0.351 / 0.287 / 0.248 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, minimum detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios = 2.67 / 2.23 / 2.00. Dropping the PD-L1 restriction enlarges the cells to roughly 65 / 121 / 450 / 837 and improves the figure to ~1.76 at f = 0.6 — but that substitutes an unrestricted comparison of two regimens chosen non-randomly on disease burden and performance status, which is a different and much weaker question, not this hypothesis.
power.adequacy: Inadequate on both counts. No mechanism in the claim graph predicts a regimen-by-STK11 interaction of 2.0-2.7-fold, and the most directly relevant recent evidence points the other way: Skoulidis 2024 argues chemo-immunotherapy is itself compromised in STK11/KEAP1-altered tumours, which would make the true interaction SMALLER than the mechanism predicts, not larger. A design that can only detect an effect the literature argues against is inadequate whatever its total N.

measurement_concerns: The workaround is worse here than for H-007 and H-008 and is refused on stronger grounds: using receipt of monotherapy as a proxy for TPS >= 50% is CIRCULAR, because regimen IS the exposure. The restriction variable and the exposure variable would be the same variable.

Exposure-dependent treatment assignment is the central threat and it is only partly addressable. days_dx_to_sequencing and treatment.start_day_offset do permit modelling whether the STK11 result was available before regimen choice, which is the right handling and is executable — but it cannot repair the missing PD-L1 restriction, and first_contact_year gives era while no site field gives the institution-level adoption gradient.
ecog_ps is nlp_extracted, nullable, and is the only frailty measure the schema offers, while being the dominant determinant of regimen intensity.

treatment.stop_day_offset must not be used to characterise regimen exposure; regimen class is determined by drug_class + regimen_id + start_day_offset within the 28-day window the hypothesis specifies.
feasibility.reject_reason: Rejected on a missing required field, with underpowering as an independent second reason. PD-L1 now exists in this schema as a binary NLP flag, so the rejection was re-derived rather than carried over — and the binary flag makes things worse here rather than better. In H-010 PD-L1 is not a covariate to be dropped; it is the restriction the hypothesis itself introduces to keep confounding by indication from consuming the estimate, and its stated purpose is to exclude TPS <50% 'where monotherapy is rarely used'. A binary 'positive' includes the 1-49% band, which is precisely where monotherapy is rarely used, so substituting it readmits the population the restriction exists to remove and reinstates the confounding it exists to defuse. The obvious alternative — treat receipt of monotherapy as evidence of TPS >= 50% — is circular, because regimen is the exposure being contrasted, and is refused rather than engineered around. Power fails on its own: the real ICI-treated STK11-LoF pool is 336 patients, which after the first-line, non-squamous, driver and regimen splits leaves roughly 65 monotherapy and 121 chemo-immunotherapy STK11-LoF patients, and roughly 36 in the chemo-immunotherapy arm once the required PD-L1 band is applied. The minimum detectable regimen-by-STK11 ratio-of-hazard-ratios is 2.23 at an assumed 60% event fraction, far above anything the mechanism predicts and pointing the opposite way to Skoulidis 2024, which argues chemo-immunotherapy is itself compromised in these tumours. Two further listed covariates, treating site and any comorbidity measure beyond nlp-extracted ECOG, are also absent — and site is exactly the variable the exposure-dependent-prescribing threat requires.

hypotheses.statement: In advanced NSCLC treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, the survival advantage normally associated with high tumour mutational burden is attenuated or absent in STK11-loss-of-function tumours relative to STK11-wildtype tumours, i.e. STK11 status modifies the TMB-benefit relationship.

origin.rationale: This is the biomarker paradox the graph states but never tests. STK11 mutation is significantly associated with HIGH TMB (C-025, and C-032 in non-smokers specifically), yet with low PD-L1 (C-041) and low CD3+/CD8+ infiltration (C-007). The mechanism that reconciles them is explicit in the graph and is what makes this an interaction rather than a curiosity: TMB is a proxy for neoantigen supply, but supply only converts into a T-cell response if the peptides are processed and presented, and LKB1 loss compromises immunoproteasome activity and raises autophagic flux, degrading exactly that step (C-031), while STING silencing removes the innate signal that would license priming (C-029). So the causal chain from TMB to benefit is cut in the middle in STK11-mutant tumours. The clinical implication is concrete and untested at scale: TMB-high should not be used to justify ICI monotherapy in an STK11-mutant tumour. A cohort with paired TMB and STK11 calls on thousands of ICI-treated patients is the only design that can estimate this interaction.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: WCLC 2018 abstract MA19.09 (J Thorac Oncol S1556-0864(18)31438-2)
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Reported that concurrent STK11 and KEAP1 mutation is associated with resistance to PD-(L)1 blockade despite high TMB. The qualitative observation is therefore eight years old and lives in a conference abstract; what has not been done is a formal TMB-by-STK11 interaction estimate with a confidence interval, or a demonstration that STK11 alone rather than the STK11/KEAP1 pair carries it.

plausibility.causal_story: TMB is a proxy for neoantigen supply, and supply converts into clinical benefit only through a chain: proteasomal processing, MHC-I loading, surface presentation, recognition by a primed CD8 repertoire, then release of the checkpoint brake. LKB1 loss degrades the processing step (reduced immunoproteasome activity, increased autophagic flux, C-031) and removes the innate licence for priming (STING silencing, C-029), so additional neoantigens do not convert into additional recognition. That is why STK11-mutant tumours are simultaneously TMB-high (C-025, C-032), PD-L1-low (C-041) and T-cell-poor (C-007). Prediction: the slope of survival benefit on TMB is flatter, or flat, within the STK11-mutant stratum. The chain also predicts specificity — TMB carries little prognostic information off checkpoint blockade — so the interaction should be ICI-specific. The falsifiable step is that presentation, rather than supply, is rate-limiting.
mechanism_steps: Higher TMB yields more candidate neoantigenic peptides.
Those peptides require immunoproteasome processing and MHC-I loading to reach the cell surface; LKB1 loss compromises exactly this step (C-031).
Priming of a naive repertoire additionally requires innate licensing through STING-dependent type I interferon, which LKB1 loss silences (C-029/C-030).
With both steps degraded, marginal neoantigen supply produces no marginal T-cell recognition in STK11-mutant tumours.
PD-1 blockade can therefore release nothing extra despite a high TMB, consistent with the observed TMB-high/PD-L1-low/T-cell-poor triad.
Prediction: a negative TMB x STK11 interaction on survival under ICI, and no comparable interaction on chemotherapy.
alternative_explanations: Smoking is a common cause of both high TMB and STK11 mutation, and the TMB-survival relationship itself differs by smoking intensity, so the interaction may be a smoking-by-TMB effect relabelled.

Measurement error: panel-derived TMB is a noisy proxy for neoantigen supply, and error in an effect modifier attenuates interaction estimates non-uniformly across strata with different TMB distributions.

Ceiling effects: the TMB-benefit relationship flattens at the top of the range in any group, and STK11-mutant tumours sit higher in that range (C-025), so an apparent slope difference may be curvature rather than modification.
confounding_risks: Panel heterogeneity: TMB is not comparable across assays, panel choice tracks institution and era, and STK11 callability varies with the same panels — so both the exposure and the modifier are measured differently across the cohort.
Smoking, as above, with pack-year data poorly captured.

Prognostic vs predictive: with no non-ICI arm, an attenuated TMB slope in STK11-mutants cannot be shown to be ICI-specific, which is the entire clinical claim (do not use TMB-high to justify monotherapy).
Correlated exposure and modifier: STK11 mutation itself raises TMB, so the STK11-mutant/TMB-low cell is sparse and the interaction rests on the least populated corner.
KEAP1 collinearity: KEAP1 also raises TMB and shortens survival, so the interaction may be carried by KEAP1 unless modelled jointly.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry; and TMB is only available for patients with adequate tissue, which correlates with disease burden and biopsy site.

missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS band — binary NLP flag only. Covariate, and one downstream of the same interferon axis as the exposure, so dropping it removes a mediator adjustment rather than a confounder adjustment. Not the reason for rejection.

Panel footprint in megabases and the TMB harmonisation method — panel_version is a categorical label and tmb_mut_per_mb is already per-megabase, but the schema exposes neither the footprint of each IMPACT version nor whether TMB was harmonised across them. The hypothesis's own inclusion criterion, 'TMB reported from a panel with a documented harmonised calculation', therefore cannot be verified from this file. This is not the reason for rejection either, but it forces the choice between a panel-restricted analysis (halving N) and an unverified comparability assumption, and both branches are computed below.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Anchored on real counts throughout. REAL: 2665 NSCLC patients received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent; of these 336 are STK11-LoF and 2329 STK11-wildtype, so the STK11-LoF fraction among ICI-treated patients is 12.6% — not the 14.1% the prior run assumed from cohort-wide prevalence. REAL: tmb_nonnull = 7809/7809, so TMB is complete and there is no missingness loss, an improvement on the prior run's assumption. REAL: by_gene_panel is IMPACT468 3919 (50.2%), IMPACT505 2228 (28.5%), IMPACT410 1336 (17.1%), IMPACT341 326 (4.2%). DERIVED: x0.85 for the EGFR/ALK exclusion (A1) gives ~2265 analysable patients, ~285 STK11-LoF and ~1980 wildtype. The prior formula-derived run put this at ~3060 analysable with ~430 STK11-mutants, from a cohort-wide 5680 ICI figure and an assumed 70% NSCLC share; the real ICI-treated NSCLC cohort is 2665 and the exposed cell is 22% smaller.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: per-SD ratio-of-hazard-ratios 1.26 at f=0.6 unrestricted; 1.38 panel-restricted; 1.60 dichotomised

power.estimand: TMB x STK11 product term on overall survival — the difference between the TMB slope inside and outside the STK11-LoF stratum, expressed as a ratio of per-standard-deviation hazard ratios for log TMB.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, reference 0.6.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: CONTINUOUS SPECIFICATION (primary). For a binary exposure X with prevalence p and a standardised continuous modifier Z, Var(beta_interaction) = 1 / (D x p(1-p)) where D is the event count. With p = 0.126 (real) and N = 2265: D = 906 / 1359 / 1812 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, SE = 0.100 / 0.082 / 0.071, minimum detectable per-SD ratio-of-hazard-ratios = 1.32 / 1.26 / 1.22. PANEL-RESTRICTED to IMPACT468 alone (a real 50.2% of NSCLC) for TMB comparability, N = 1137: 1.47 / 1.38 / 1.32. DICHOTOMISED at a TMB-high threshold (q ~ 0.4), residual variance p(1-p)q(1-q) = 0.0264: SE = 0.167 at f = 0.6, minimum detectable ratio 1.60, because the STK11-LoF/TMB-low corner is the sparse one — STK11 mutation itself raises TMB, so the interaction rests on the least populated cell. Prior run reported 1.25 continuous panel-restricted and passed on it; the same calculation on the real cohort gives 1.38 panel-restricted and 1.26 unrestricted.
power.adequacy: Inadequate, and this is the verdict that changed from the prior run. The judgement turns on writing out what effect size the hypothesis actually predicts, which the prior run asserted rather than computed. The estimand is the ratio of the per-SD log-TMB hazard ratio in STK11-mutants to that in STK11-wildtype patients. Within-ICI-arm TMB associations with overall survival in NSCLC are modest: a per-SD hazard ratio of roughly 0.80-0.85 in the wildtype stratum is a fair reading of the published range. The hypothesis predicts the slope is 'attenuated or absent' in STK11-mutants; TOTAL abolition — the strongest form of the claim, HR 1.0 — is then a ratio of only 1.18 to 1.25, which sits BELOW the 1.26 detection threshold at the reference event fraction and below the 1.38 threshold if TMB comparability forces the panel restriction. The design can detect the predicted effect only if the wildtype TMB slope is far steeper than the literature supports (a per-SD HR near 0.73 or below), i.e. only by assuming away the thing that makes the interaction small. This is the four-times-the-events rule biting exactly where the stage brief said it hides: 2265 patients look ample for a main effect and are not ample for an interaction at 12.6% exposure prevalence. The prior run's contrary conclusion rested on an inflated cohort (3060 with 430 mutants against a real 2265 with 285) and on the unexamined assertion that the mechanism implies an effect 'well beyond 1.25-fold'. It does not.

measurement_concerns: Exposure and modifier are both genomic, not NLP — this hypothesis's ascertainment is good and that is not why it dies.

tmb_mut_per_mb is complete (7809/7809, real) but completeness is not comparability. Four panel footprints (IMPACT341/410/468/505, real distribution above) produce TMB estimates that are not interchangeable, and panel choice tracks institution and era while STK11 callability varies with the same panels. Restricting to the dominant panel halves N and moves the detectable effect from 1.26 to 1.38; not restricting requires an unverifiable harmonisation assumption. Neither branch reaches adequacy, which is why the panel question does not need resolving.

Measurement error in an effect modifier attenuates an interaction non-uniformly across strata with different modifier distributions, and STK11-LoF tumours sit higher in the TMB range — so any observed flattening is partly ceiling and curvature rather than modification. A flexible functional form would be needed and would cost further precision.

smoking_status and pack_years are nlp_extracted and are the dominant common cause of both high TMB and STK11 mutation; they are covariates here, not the exposure, but they cannot be measured better in this dataset.

KEAP1 collinearity: KEAP1 also raises TMB and shortens survival, and the real STK11-KEAP1 co-occurrence is 50.5% (512/1013), so joint modelling is required and would consume further degrees of freedom in an already-marginal interaction.

Left truncation at days_dx_to_sequencing required, and the any-line population makes it worse than for the first-line hypotheses because the time origin and the sequencing date can fall in either order.
feasibility.reject_reason: Underpowered for the interaction the hypothesis actually predicts. This verdict CHANGED from the prior stage-4 run, and the change is entirely attributable to the schema going from formula-derived to real. The prior run derived ~3060 analysable ICI-treated NSCLC patients with ~430 STK11-mutants from a cohort-wide ICI count and an assumed NSCLC share; the real figures are 2665 ICI-treated NSCLC patients with 336 STK11-LoF among them, so the exposed cell is 22% smaller and the exposure prevalence is 12.6% rather than 14.1%. On the same continuous specification the minimum detectable per-SD ratio-of-hazard-ratios is 1.26 at an assumed 60% event fraction unrestricted, 1.38 if TMB comparability forces restriction to IMPACT468 (a real 50.2% of the cohort), and 1.60 if TMB is dichotomised. Set against that: the estimand is the ratio of the per-SD TMB hazard ratio in STK11-mutants to that in wildtype patients, and within-ICI-arm TMB slopes in NSCLC correspond to a per-SD hazard ratio of roughly 0.80-0.85, so COMPLETE abolition of the slope in STK11-mutants — the strongest form of the claim — is a ratio of only 1.18-1.25. The design cannot detect it. The prior run passed this on the assertion that the mechanism implies an effect 'well beyond 1.25-fold'; that assertion was never converted into a number, and when it is, it is false for any plausible wildtype slope. This is the interaction-needs-four-times-the-events rule biting where the brief said it hides: 2265 patients is a comfortable main-effect cohort and an inadequate interaction cohort at 12.6% exposure prevalence. The clinical claim the hypothesis exists to support — that TMB-high should not justify ICI monotherapy in an STK11-mutant tumour — is too consequential to rest on an interval that cannot exclude the null under the hypothesis's own best case. Sent to the graveyard rather than to pre-registration, with the note that it becomes viable in a cohort with roughly four times these ICI-treated numbers, or in a pooled multi-institution analysis.

hypotheses.statement: In a first-line advanced NSCLC population analysed with a time-to-event rather than a binary endpoint, STK11 loss-of-function is associated with a modestly shorter time to progression or death on anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, an association the PIONeeR primary-resistance analysis was structurally unable to detect.

origin.rationale: PIONeeR is the most rigorous negative in the graph: a prospective multicentre biomarker cohort in which STK11 was neither associated with primary resistance (OR 1.17, 0.634-2.17, p-adj 0.896) nor with PFS (C-046). It deserves to be taken seriously, and it is also the kind of null worth re-testing with a named fix rather than dismissing. Three specific features limit it. First, the primary endpoint is a binary primary-resistance label, and dichotomising a time-to-event outcome discards most of the information — with 58 STK11-mutant patients, an odds ratio of 1.17 is compatible with a hazard ratio in the 1.2-1.4 range that the pooled literature reports (C-039, HR 1.45). Second, the population is second-line-plus, where survivorship has already selected against the aggressive phenotype (this is the same effect H-006 tests directly). Third, p-values are adjusted across a large multimodal biomarker panel, which is correct for discovery but heavily penalises a prespecified single hypothesis. The fix is therefore explicit: a first-line population, a time-to-event endpoint, no multiplicity penalty from unrelated biomarkers, and adjustment for PD-L1 and smoking. I expect a small, real, and prognostic-looking effect rather than the large predictive one the early literature claims.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: The null being re-tested. 439 patients enrolled, 305 sequenced, 58 STK11-mutant; STK11 OR 1.17 (0.634-2.17), AUC 0.54, p-adjusted 0.896, and no PFS association. Preprint, not peer reviewed. If a larger first-line time-to-event analysis also returns null, the STK11 resistance claim is in serious trouble and this hypothesis should die loudly rather than quietly.

In first-line immunotherapy, STK11 gave OS HR 1.4 (0.9-2.3, p=0.1) — nonsignificant, and identical in point estimate to the HR 1.4 (1.2-1.6) seen in the first-line chemotherapy arm of the same cohort. A second, larger, first-line null on the ICI side that also points to prognosis rather than prediction.

plausibility.causal_story: None is offered. The stated chain runs: PIONeeR dichotomised its endpoint and adjusted p-values across many biomarkers, therefore it had low sensitivity; therefore a time-to-event first-line analysis will detect a modest effect. Those are claims about estimator behaviour, not about biology. The implied biological content — LKB1 loss shortens time to progression — is the association itself, and the mechanisms that would explain it (C-029, C-031) are neither invoked nor used to generate any prediction that separates this hypothesis from the prognostic account or from H-001.
mechanism_steps: Dichotomising a time-to-event outcome into a binary resistance label discards information and lowers power. (Statistical, not biological.)
Second-line populations are survivorship-selected, attenuating prognostic effects. (Selection, not mechanism — and the content of H-006.)
Multiplicity adjustment across an unrelated biomarker panel penalises a prespecified single hypothesis. (Analytic choice.)
Therefore a first-line time-to-event analysis will show a modest STK11 association. (Restatement of the correlation; no biological step is required for this to be true or false.)
alternative_explanations: The association is entirely prognostic — the same point estimate appears on first-line chemotherapy with no ICI present (C-037, HR 1.4) — so a positive result here would be uninformative about checkpoint blockade.
Residual confounding by PD-L1, smoking and performance status produces a modest hazard ratio of the size predicted without any LKB1-specific effect.
Selection into sequencing: patients sequenced before or early in first-line therapy differ systematically from those sequenced later, and STK11 prevalence tracks tissue adequacy and panel breadth.
confounding_risks: Prognostic vs predictive is unresolvable by construction: no non-ICI arm, so a within-ICI hazard ratio is exactly the estimand the field already has and cannot interpret.

Surveillance bias on a progression endpoint: real-world imaging intervals are irregular and clinicians who know a patient carries a resistance-associated genotype scan sooner, which inflates measured progression rates in the exposed group independently of biology.
Interval censoring: progression dates are ascertained at scan dates, so short-horizon differences are quantised by scheduling patterns that differ across sites and eras.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry, which is acute for a first-line PFS endpoint because sequencing frequently reports after treatment start.
Smoking and PD-L1 as the leading measured confounders, both incompletely captured.
Panel ascertainment: STK11 callability varies by assay, so the comparator group is contaminated with untested patients.
plausibility.reject_reason: There is no causal story here, only a measurement argument. Every reason given for expecting the association — dichotomisation of a time-to-event outcome, a second-line population, multiplicity adjustment across an unrelated biomarker panel — concerns how PIONeeR was analysed, not what LKB1 does. The statement itself, 'STK11 loss-of-function is associated with a modestly shorter time to progression or death on anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy', restates the correlation the field has already pooled across 14 studies and 4,317 patients (C-039, PFS HR 1.45). No step is proposed that could be false about biology, and no differential prediction is made: the candidate's own expectation is 'a small, real, and prognostic-looking effect', which by construction cannot distinguish prediction from prognosis in a design with no non-ICI comparator. H-001 asks the same underlying question with the comparator arm that makes it answerable; H-012 is that design with the discriminating contrast deleted, so it tests nothing H-001 does not test better. A methodological improvement on a prior null is a good reason to re-analyse someone else's data; it is not a hypothesis.

hypotheses.statement: In resectable NSCLC treated with neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy, KRAS/STK11 co-mutation is associated with shorter recurrence-free survival after resection without a correspondingly lower major pathologic response rate, i.e. pathologic response and durable disease control dissociate in this genotype.

origin.rationale: The graph contains a within-study dissociation nobody has the power to interpret: in the same tiny neoadjuvant cohort, KRAS/STK11 co-mutants had an RFS hazard ratio of 7.09 (p=0.027, n=52) while major pathologic response was 17% versus 25% (p=1.0, n=21, seven co-mutants). The MPR null is the buried negative — a nonsignificant result in a 21-patient comparison that would be read as reassurance. The reason to believe the dissociation is real rather than noise is mechanistic and testable: major pathologic response after neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is driven substantially by the cytotoxic component, which LKB1 loss does not impair, whereas durable freedom from recurrence depends on immune control of residual microscopic disease, which requires the antigen presentation (C-031) and functional CD8 response (C-036 reports CD8 dysfunction rather than absence in STK11-deficient tumours) that LKB1 loss degrades. If that is right, MPR is a poor surrogate endpoint specifically in this genotype — which matters because MPR is increasingly used as the trial-level surrogate in the perioperative setting. Only a cohort linking genomics to surgical pathology and long-term recurrence at scale can test it.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: PMID 39545922 (Rosner et al., Clin Cancer Res 2025;31:339-51)
prior_negative_evidence.summary: The primary report behind C-044/C-045 already describes significantly shorter RFS in KRAS-mutant/STK11-mutant tumours despite comparable pathologic response rates, with supporting bulk RNA sequencing on the tumour immune microenvironment. The dissociation is therefore published, not undiscovered, and novelty here is limited to replication with adequate power — the primary cohort had roughly seven co-mutant patients. Recorded because it substantially discounts this candidate.

Reports that KRAS and STK11 mutations shape the CD8+ T-cell response in resectable NSCLC after neoadjuvant therapy, supplying the immunologic correlate but again in a small surgical series with no independent RFS validation.

proposed_covariates: clinical stage before neoadjuvant therapy and pathologic stage at resection
extent of resection and margin status

plausibility.causal_story: As proposed: platinum drives bulk tumour regression and hence major pathologic response, a process LKB1 loss does not impair, while freedom from recurrence depends on immune control of residual microscopic disease requiring antigen presentation (C-031) and functional CD8 responses (C-036) that LKB1 loss degrades; hence a dissociation, and hence MPR is a poor surrogate in this genotype. The first step fails: in neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy the pathologic response is largely the immunotherapy's contribution, so the same defect that impairs durable control should also impair pathologic response. With that step removed the mechanism predicts concordance, and the observed 'dissociation' reduces to a nonsignificant comparison in 21 patients read as evidence.
mechanism_steps: Neoadjuvant platinum doublet causes bulk cytoreduction independent of LKB1 status. (True in isolation.)

Major pathologic response therefore mainly measures the cytotoxic effect. (FALSE for chemo-immunotherapy: the pathologic response gain over chemotherapy alone is attributable to the checkpoint inhibitor.)
Durable freedom from recurrence requires immune surveillance of residual microscopic disease via MHC-I presentation and functional CD8 memory (C-031, C-036).
LKB1 loss degrades that surveillance, shortening recurrence-free survival.
Therefore recurrence-free survival is reduced while pathologic response is preserved. (Does not follow once step 2 is corrected; the corrected chain predicts both are reduced.)
alternative_explanations: The MPR null is sampling noise: 17% vs 25% with p=1.0 in 21 patients has an interval spanning almost the entire plausible range, so 'no difference' is uninformative rather than a buried negative.
The RFS signal is small-cell instability: HR 7.09 from roughly seven co-mutant patients is the kind of estimate that regresses hard toward the null on replication.

Stage and adjuvant-therapy imbalance: co-mutant patients may present with higher pathologic stage and receive different adjuvant treatment, which drives recurrence-free survival without any surrogate-endpoint dissociation.
confounding_risks: Surveillance intensity determines recurrence detection, and imaging frequency after resection varies by site, stage and clinician concern — a direct route to differential ascertainment of the RFS endpoint.
Selection into resection: patients who progress during neoadjuvant therapy never reach surgery, which removes the worst-outcome exposed patients and distorts both endpoints in opposite directions.
Pathologic response assessment is not standardised across institutions, and residual-viable-tumour scoring is observer-dependent.
Adjuvant therapy receipt after resection is a post-baseline variable on the causal path to recurrence.
Immortal time between diagnosis, sequencing and resection.

Prognostic vs predictive: no non-immunotherapy neoadjuvant comparator exists in current practice, so the surrogate-failure claim cannot be attributed to the ICI component even if the dissociation were observed.
plausibility.reject_reason: The dissociation requires that major pathologic response after neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is driven by the cytotoxic component and is therefore LKB1-independent. That premise is false: pathologic response in this setting is overwhelmingly attributable to the checkpoint inhibitor added to chemotherapy — pathologic complete response rises roughly tenfold when anti-PD-1 is added to neoadjuvant platinum doublet, against a low single-digit rate for chemotherapy alone. So the very antigen-presentation and priming defects the hypothesis invokes to explain the recurrence-free survival deficit (C-031, C-029, C-036) predict a LOWER major pathologic response rate as well. Followed honestly, the mechanism predicts concordance between the two endpoints, not the claimed dissociation. The other limb is worse: 'no correspondingly lower MPR' rests on 17% versus 25% with p=1.0 in 21 patients, of whom 7 were co-mutant (C-045). Sampling noise is a complete explanation for that null and no biology is needed. The RFS limb (C-044, HR 7.09) comes from a review restating a primary report the mapper never opened, in a cohort of the same 7 co-mutants. Building a surrogate-endpoint claim on a seven-patient cell whose non-significant arm is treated as a finding inverts the evidence.

hypotheses.statement: Biallelic STK11 inactivation is associated with shorter overall survival on ICI-containing therapy than monoallelic or missense-only STK11 alteration, and monoallelic missense STK11 alteration behaves like STK11 wild-type.

origin.rationale: This is the established-mechanism-whose-clinical-implication-was-never-tested case, and it may be the single best explanation for why the graph disagrees with itself. LKB1 is a classic two-hit tumour suppressor, and every mechanism in the graph — STING silencing via SAM/DNMT1/EZH2 (C-029, C-030) and loss of immunoproteasome-dependent presentation (C-031) — requires the kinase activity to be gone, not merely reduced. Li et al. make the same argument from the other direction, showing the transcriptomic STK11-deficient phenotype rather than mutation status identifies ICB-refractory tumours (C-034), with the companion claim that tissue mutation alone does not (C-035, unverified and so discounted here). Every clinical cohort in the graph defines exposure as 'STK11 mutated', pooling true biallelic loss with heterozygous missense variants of uncertain effect. That non-differential-looking but actually directional misclassification would attenuate estimates toward the null and would do so by different amounts in cohorts with different panel content and different variant-calling thresholds — which is exactly the pattern of disagreement seen between Skoulidis, Papillon-Cavanagh, the Japanese C-CAT cohort and PIONeeR, and it also fits the unexplained prevalence spread from 8.6% to 25% (C-048). A cohort with copy-number and zygosity calls alongside mutation calls can separate the strata; no published cohort in this graph has.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: J Thorac Oncol S1556-0864(24)00081-9, 'Precision Immunotherapy for STK11/KEAP1-Mutant NSCLC'
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Review that already argues clonality, allelic status and variant class should stratify treatment: it states that clonal mutations with LOH in KEAP1, unlike subclonal ones, associate with resistance and a T-cell-excluded microenvironment, and recommends that subclonal or benign-predicted missense variants with high PD-L1 should not be steered away from PD-(L)1 monotherapy. The idea is therefore in print for KEAP1; the STK11-specific effect estimate is what is missing, which is what the mapper independently found in coverage note 6.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: J Thorac Oncol S1556-0864(25)00049-8, 'Gene Copy Deletion of STK11, KEAP1, and SMARCA4: Clinicopathologic Features and Association With the Outcomes of Immunotherapy With or Without Chemotherapy in Nonsquamous NSCLC'
prior_negative_evidence.summary: A 2025 study that specifically addresses copy deletion of STK11 and immunotherapy outcomes — the closest existing work to this hypothesis. The full text returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval so its effect estimates and whether it separated biallelic from monoallelic events could not be confirmed; it must be read before this candidate is pre-registered, and it may substantially reduce or eliminate the gap.

Argues from transcriptomic phenotype that mutation status is a poor proxy for functional STK11 loss, and reports the phenotype rather than the mutation identifies ICB-refractory tumours. Supports the premise but also means the 'mutation is a poor proxy' claim is established; the novelty is in using zygosity as a genomic proxy for the functional state, which a clinicogenomic dataset can compute and a transcriptomic signature cannot.

exposure.genomic_criteria: STK11 homozygous deletion, or a truncating variant (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site) together with loss of heterozygosity or a second qualifying variant at the STK11 locus; where available, high variant allele fraction adjusted for tumour purity is used as the supporting zygosity signal
exposure.treatment_criteria: first-line ICI-containing therapy, regimen class entered as a covariate

comparator.description: Two explicit comparator strata rather than one: (a) monoallelic STK11 alteration, defined as a single truncating or oncogenic missense variant with retained heterozygosity, and (b) STK11 wild-type. The hypothesis predicts stratum (a) resembles stratum (b) and both differ from the exposed group.

inclusion: copy-number or LOH information available at STK11
tumour purity estimate available or variant allele fraction reported
